reason: The hypothesis directly applies the well-established SPS approach for ZrB2 (P20, P4, P7, P14, P30, P43, P46) and the known mechanism of low-temperature densification via plastic deformation (P5, P6, P8, P18, P19, P49) to predict improved mechanical integrity and durability in a liquid plating bath. This is a straightforward extension of existing results to a new service environment without combining disparate findings, proposing a new mechanism, or resolving a conflict; the core idea is a textbook application of SPS to a known material.
copied_elements: lower sintering temperature reduces grain growth and porosity (P1, P5, P6, P8, P18, P19, P49)
rapid heating and short dwell times in SPS (P20, P30)
enhanced densification via plastic deformation/dislocation mechanisms (P5, P6, P8, P49)
improved mechanical properties (hardness, fracture toughness) from denser, finer-grained ZrB2 (P1, P2, P3, P7, P13, P14, P19, P27, P28, P34, P42, P46)
liquid plating bath exposure as a service condition (general knowledge)
